newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Plane carrying Australia PM hit by lightning.
newsitem.headline: Plane carrying Australia PM hit by lightning.

text.p: An aircraft carrying Australian Prime Minister John Howard made an emergency landing after being struck by lightning on Thursday, a spokesman for Howard's office said.
No one on board was injured, government spokesman David Gazard told Reuters by telephone from Canberra.

The incident occurred about 15 minutes after the 14-seater Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) Falcon jet carrying Howard and about a dozen other people left Canberra for the southern island state of Tasmania at about 7.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).
"No one was hurt but one of the people on board said there was a very intense, blinding flash of light across the plane," Gazard said.
"Obviously, they were shocked enough that the prime minister immediately called his wife after the plane returned to Canberra to tell her he was all right," he said.
RAAF engineers inspected the plane after it landed in Canberra and declared it unsafe after finding a hole about the size of a small coin in the plane's nose cone where the lightning had struck.

Howard transferred to another RAAF Falcon used by government ministers and travelled on to Hobart, capital of Tasmania, where he will attend a meeting of his Liberal Party's federal council beginning Friday.
